Hi Mina,

Hope you're well — we're doing a privacy assessment ahead of our pilot and I was asked to get a few confirmations from vendors. Two short items for Redwood: 

1) Our site includes marketing pixels and a few analytics endpoints. Can you provide a current cookie/pixel inventory that lists the domains the pixels call out to, what data is sent (e.g., IP, user-agent, email hash), and whether any identifiers are persisted client-side?

2) Because we handle PHI at NexaHealth, our privacy team wants to confirm whether Redwood's hosted inference platform can be configured to prevent PHI transmission through client-side telemetry (i.e., browser JS). If browser-side SDKs/embedded widgets are used, are there safeguards or recommended patterns?

Bonus ask: for EU visitors we need: a) confirmation that transfers outside the EEA are covered by SCCs or other mechanism, and b) any DPA/DPIA artifacts you can share (a redacted DPIA or a template would help).

Can you send over a pack of documents or point me to a drive link? We have a compliance checkpoint Friday 4/23, so if possible we'd like materials this week.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Privacy Program Manager
NexaHealth

Hi Elena,

Thanks for the clear list — happy to help. Quick answers and I'll loop in security for the tech details: 

- Cookie/pixel inventory: attached is a current export (cookie-inventory-20260418.csv) and a short inventory explaining destinations and common payloads. In summary, our hosted UI loads a marketing analytics pixel (analytics.global-redwood.com) and a support chat widget (chat.partnerco.com). The marketing pixel receives hashed identifiers only when a customer explicitly configures identity sync; otherwise it only receives anonymized session-level signals (IP truncated for geolocation precision).

- PHI via browser telemetry: our public SDKs are opt-in; we strongly recommend tokenization at the application layer and explicit client-side redaction. By default, the SDK will not sample request bodies nor send model inputs unless the customer enables telemetry collection. We can provide a recommended config policy for NexaHealth to enforce no-client-PII collection.

- Data transfers / SCCs / DPIA: I have a signed DPA link and a SOC 2 summary I can share now. For SCCs and DPIA artifacts we need to involve legal/security for the DPIA template and any redacted examples — I'll loop them in.

I'm including a short pack: redwood_soc2-summary.pdf (high-level), cookie-inventory-20260418.csv, and a stub link to our signed DPA (redwood_dpa_signed_link.txt). Will follow up after I sync with Aditya on the DPIA/SCC specifics.

Mina / Marissa — quick answers and artifacts attached. TL;DR: we can support a no-PHI-in-transit posture for NexaHealth with configuration and contract controls. Details: 

- Destinations and identifiers: The marketing analytics endpoint (analytics.global-redwood.com) is hosted across multi-region infra; production ingestion endpoints for marketing signals are served from both EU and US regions depending on request routing. By default the SDK does NOT send email or clear-text identifiers; email_hash is only sent when customers enable identity sync. I've attached a mapping table (redwood_data_field_map.txt) that enumerates fields and which downstream systems ingest them.

- Server-side telemetry & logs: If NexaHealth disables client-side SDKs and does not forward identifiers in API requests, the only server-side artifacts that could include user-level metadata are access logs (IP, timestamp, path) and request headers. Model inputs/outputs are not logged in plaintext in production; we redact or store only as encrypted blobs per our retention policy. Retention windows: access logs 30 days; audit traces 90 days (redwood_soc2-summary.pdf has more).

- SCCs / DPIA: We have standard SCCs in our DPA for EEA transfers and a DPIA template. I'll attach the CAIQ snapshot and a redacted DPIA template; legal will need to sign off on redactions.

I'll push a consolidated zip to Drive and confirm the DPA/SCC linkage by EOD.

—Aditya Rao
Principal Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
